newsitem.title: USA: U.S. firms "absorb" wage hikes so far -Fed's Meyer.
newsitem.headline: U.S. firms "absorb" wage hikes so far -Fed's Meyer.

text.p: Global competition has forced U.S. corporations "to absorb" some costs incurred by boosting wages without corresponding hikes in prices, but the Federal Reserve is ready to respond if that trend does not continue, Federal Reserve Governor Laurence Meyer said on Sunday.

"The question is whether the recent wage gains will in fact prove to be real in terms of greater effective purchasing power or whether the associated increases in cost of production will only be mirrored in an offsetting accelleration of prices," Meyer told the National Association of Business Economists.
In an addendum to a speech prepared before Friday's release of the August employment report, Meyer said the U.S. Central bank is ready to respond to any wage-related inflationary risk.
He said U.S. corporations so far "have been forced by competittive conditions to absorb some of them (wage gains) in their profit margins."
He added, "The question is whether these profits will continue in the months ahead."

In an apparent reference to the August jobs data that included a spike in average hourly earnings, Meyers said "the latest data reinforced" a view recently expressed by Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan: "that we are in a circumstance in which a prudent central bank must exercise heightened surveilance of the inflationary risk."
Meyer said he trusts the Fed will "stand ready to respond if necessary." The next scheduled meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee, which sets monetary policy, is for Sept. 24.
